text: You, however, must teach what agrees with sound doctrine.
Older men are to be temperate, dignified, self-controlled, sound in faith, in love, and in endurance.
Older women, likewise, are to be reverent in the way they live, not slanderers or slaves to heavy drinking, but teachers of what is good.
so that they may train the younger women to love their husbands and to love their children,

versions.text: In this way they will train the younger women to love their husbands and their children,
versions.explanation: The Greek ἵνα introduces a purpose clause dependent on verse 3, but the current rendering turns it into an independent result statement ("In this way they will"). Restoring "so that they may train" keeps the grammatical link with the previous verse and matches the sense of σωφρονίζωσι. Repeating "to love" also mirrors the two distinct terms φιλάνδρους and φιλοτέκνους and reads well aloud.

text: to be self-controlled and pure, to be busy at home, to be kind, and to submit to their own husbands, so that the word of God may not be dishonored.

versions.text: to be self-controlled and pure, to manage their households well, to be kind, and to submit to their own husbands, so that no one will speak evil of the word of God.
versions.explanation: οἰκουργούς means "working at home" rather than "managing the household well" (which would render a different term); and the final clause is passive in Greek with no stated agent, so "no one will speak evil" adds an agent not present in the text. The suggested wording stays closer to the Greek while remaining smooth for reading aloud.

text: Urge the younger men, in the same way, to be self-controlled.
In everything, make yourself a model of good works. In your teaching show integrity and dignity,
and let your message be sound and beyond reproach, so that any opponent will be put to shame, having nothing bad to say about us.
Slaves are to submit to their masters in everything, to be well pleasing, not argumentative,
not stealing from them, but showing themselves completely trustworthy, so that in every way they may bring credit to the teaching of God our Savior.
For the grace of God has appeared, bringing salvation to all people.
It trains us to renounce godlessness and worldly desires, and to live self-controlled, upright, and godly lives in the present age,
as we wait for the blessed hope—the appearing of the glory of our great God and Savior, Jesus Christ.
He gave himself for us to redeem us from all lawlessness and to purify for himself a people of his own, eager to do good works.
These are the things you are to teach; encourage and rebuke with full authority. Let no one look down on you.
